text:
maya: quick heads-up — noticed repeated 20–80ms tail spikes on small-seq requests during high qps bursts on prod-rt pool, looks correlated with kernel swap to non-Flash attention when paged-KV hits spike.

maya: repro steps:
- run the small-seq canary load (seq_len ~ 32, tokens/op ~ 40) against model-x on pool A
- ramp to 12k rps for 30s, then steady 6k
- observe per-token latency distribution on trace (see perf dash)

maya: profiler snippet (sampling, simplified):
```
2026-03-15T11:12:23Z sample: batcher: forming 3 slots -> kernel select: flashattention ok
2026-03-15T11:12:24Z sample: sudden paged-kv pagefault spike -> switch kernel path -> NN_KERNEL_ATTENTION_GENERIC + fallback
2026-03-15T11:12:24Z sample: batch size 2 -> token_budget hit -> queue slotting collapsed -> latency +45ms
```

alex: interesting — so pagefaults in paged-KV are tipping kernel selector to non-Flash path and the batcher doesn't re-slot until token_budget window clears?

zheng: correct, seen this locally. Kernel selector uses a cheap heuristic: if paged_kv_faults > X within the last 100ms we mark kernel as "paged_unfriendly" for that device and pick generic kernels. That decision currently doesn't bubble into the continuous batcher slot allocator fast enough.

sam: what's our current token_budget target for small-seq? IIRC we target 512 tokens per slot, with 3 slots default on 8-GPU pool.

maya: yes: token_budget_per_slot=512, max_slots=3. But when pagefault spikes we drop effective throughput and the queue tends to merge small requests into 1–2 slots -> long head-of-line for the rest.

alex: two immediate ideas: (1) make kernel selector emit a transient confidence score so batcher can decide to keep smaller slot_width (avoid collapsing) (2) fast path to prioritize Flash kernels when safe by pinning recent-kernel-decisions for Nms even if pagefaults transiently occur.

zheng: +1 on confidence score. It should be cheap: e.g. return {kernel: flash, conf: 0.6} and we treat conf < 0.7 as 'probable fallback' and keep slotting conservative. We can tweak threshold per-model.

maya: also we should consider reducing token_budget_per_slot adaptively when paged-KV fault-rate > threshold. Quick patch idea: when KV_fault_rate > 0.05 faults/op over 500ms, set token_budget_per_slot *= 0.6 and max_slots=4 to keep latency stable.

sam: increasing max_slots to 4 helps fairness but could increase scheduling overhead. We need a microbenchmark. Can we run a quick A/B on canary pool?

perfbot: automated test queued: perf/canary/slotting-adaptive-2026-03-15 -> scheduled on pool-canary-2 at 2026-03-15T12:00:00Z. Results will post here.

maya: here's a short config patch I'm going to try on canary (pseudo-rc):
```
batcher.adaptive_token_budget.enabled = true
batcher.adaptive_token_budget.window_ms = 500
batcher.adaptive_token_budget.kv_fault_threshold = 0.05
batcher.adaptive_token_budget.scale = 0.6
batcher.slotting.max_slots = 4
kernel.selector.emit_confidence = true
```

zheng: please also add a metric: kernel_confidence_ratio and expose it in the per-device trace so we can correlate with long-tail spikes.

alex: when you run canary, add a short trace that dumps kernel selection decision per invocation (just kernel name + conf + kv_faults) — format: `KS:flash:0.63:kv_faults=0.08` so we can grep.

maya: will do. Running now on pool-canary-2 with load script `./scripts/canary_smallseq_ramp.sh --rps 12k --dur 45s`.

oncall-bot: deploy started by maya to pool-canary-2 (deploy id d-9e7f). ETA ~ 2m.

maya: first run finished, initial glance: 95th latency down from 128ms -> 88ms, tail still has a few spikes at 210ms but frequency reduced. Posting full log to gist in a sec.

sam: thanks — do we have a regression risk where confidence scoring prevents fallback when fallback is required and causes OOM or correctness issues? Need guardrails.

zheng: yes we must ensure functional correctness: kernel selector must still fall back if hardware K failures occur. Confidence-only affects batcher heuristics, not actual kernel enforcement. Batcher treats low conf as a signal to keep smaller slots, it won't override kernel safety checks.

maya: uploaded logs: https://internal.perf.redwood/p/slotting-adaptive-1767890123 -> contains traces and per-invocation KS lines.

alex: I grepped traces: majority of KS lines with conf < 0.7 coincide with paged-KV pagefault bursts. Looks promising. I'd like another run with slightly higher kv_fault_threshold (0.08) to see stability tradeoff.

maya: queued run with kv_fault_threshold=0.08 and scale=0.5. perfbot will post results.

perfbot: perf/canary/slotting-adaptive-2026-03-15-run2 -> PASS (latency p95 improved, cpu overhead +3%), artifacts: https://internal.perf.redwood/p/slotting-adaptive-1767890123-run2

sam: small note: the extra CPU is from slotting bookkeeping and more slots. Cost trade-off looks reasonable compared to p95 improvement.

zheng: next steps: (1) land kernel.selector.emit_confidence as opt-in flag, (2) land adaptive token budget with feature flag per-pool, (3) add per-model tuning docs and a small automation to suggest thresholds based on historical kv_fault_rate.

maya: I'm going to open a PR with the canary config and the kernel-confidence API. Will tag you all.

alex: thanks — if we get consistent green on 48h canary we should roll to prod-rt with slow rollout + monitor rule on kernel_confidence_ratio.

maya: ACK. I'll set up the dashboard alarms: alert if kernel_confidence_ratio < 0.6 for >2m AND p95 > 150ms.

oncall-bot: reminder: postmortem template auto-created for any incident > 5min; no incident created for these runs.

maya: closing for now — will update thread with PR link and final canary graphs. :thumbsup:
